findings.note: The synonymity pair 'glove puppet/hand puppet' and the concealment pair 'glove/hand' share the same two root words, so a player scanning the board will feel these four terms belong together and may mis-slot 'glove' or 'hand' into the wrong set.

Flipping the right pair to audition:polish (or equivalently the left pair) gives start:finish on both sides, so rough-cut:curtain call :: audition:polish reads as a consistent earlier-to-later analogy. Both halves read as: "start-of-editing to finish-of-production (start:finish)" and "start-of-production to finish-of-editing, i.e. audition:polish read as start:finish".
car : auto reads the same as auto : car — naming one thing twice is mutual
Marionette/string puppet and glove puppet/hand puppet are pure synonym pairs, so nothing in the words themselves fixes which name leads in each pair.

notes:
Fix cross-set word reuse between synonymity and concealment sets (glove/hand), fix the invalid alternate reading in before-after set, and resolve unfixable order-ambiguity in synonymity's synonym pairs.
- set-concealment: 'glove'/'hand' duplicate the root words of 'glove puppet'/'hand puppet' in set-synonymity, creating a plausible alternate analogy across the two sets.
  Try: Replace the pair ['glove','hand'] with a different concealment pair not sharing roots with any puppet-type name, e.g. ['mask','face'] or ['veil','face']
  Or: Keep ['blacks','puppeteer'] and pair it with ['curtain','stage'] or ['sheath','blade'] instead of glove/hand
  Or: If glove/hand must stay, change set-synonymity's pair to avoid 'glove puppet'/'hand puppet' entirely, e.g. replace with 'fantoccini : string puppet' style non-overlapping synonym pair
- set-before-after: The pairs cross-read validly as audition:polish::rough-cut:curtain call, since both sides are just start/finish stages from different processes, not a single shared span.
  Try: Replace 'audition'/'curtain call' with a pair from the same single production span as rough-cut/polish, e.g. 'sketch : finished sculpture' or 'draft : final cut'
  Or: Replace 'rough-cut'/'polish' with a stage-production pair matching audition/curtain call's domain and span, e.g. 'rehearsal : opening night'
  Or: Choose two pairs whose start/finish anchors are domain-specific and non-interchangeable, e.g. 'seedling : harvest' and 'sketch : polish'
- set-synonymity: Both pairs are pure symmetric synonyms with no cue for which word leads, so order is unguessable/arbitrary (car:auto issue).
  Try: Replace one or both pairs with synonym pairs that have a clear register/specificity direction, e.g. 'technical term : common term' such as 'marotte : rod puppet' with rod puppet as the more common label leading
  Or: Add a consistent directional framing in the relationship label (e.g. 'technical name : common name') and reorder pairs so the technical term always comes first, e.g. 'string puppet : marionette' and 'hand puppet : glove puppet'
  Or: Swap to pairs where one term is clearly the broader/umbrella term and the other the specific term, establishing a non-arbitrary order
Do not change: set-agent-instrument — no allowlisted finding touches them.

persisted.note: Both halves compare the same string-vs-hand category split, just at different naming registers, so a player can read this as a consistent analogy even though the intended relation is common-to-technical within each pair. Both halves read as: "sibling puppet-type distinction (string vs hand), named with common terms" and "the same sibling puppet-type distinction (string vs hand), named with technical terms".

Flipping the right pair to sketch:polish gives an earlier-to-later shaping relation matching rough-cut:finished sculpture, so a player following the general 'rough form to finished form' progression can solve this reading. Both halves read as: "rough-cut before finished sculpture (earlier stage to later stage)" and "sketch before polish, read in reverse as sketch:polish (earlier stage to later stage)".
car : auto reads the same as auto : car — naming one thing twice is mutual
Both pairs are pure synonyms with no inherent directional order (nothing marks one term as 'prior' to the other), so the order A:B::C:D was chosen arbitrarily rather than read from the words.
